subject: history_social
passage: The scholar al-Biruni, who traveled into northwestern India in the early eleventh century in the train of the armies of Mahmud of Ghazni, spent years learning Sanskrit and questioning Indian astronomers, mathematicians, and priests before composing his great description of the country's learning and customs. He announced at the outset that he would report what Indians themselves believed, in their own terms, and leave readers to judge; where he disagreed, he said so separately. Modern historians, who must otherwise rely on the far more partisan chronicles of the conquerors, value the work precisely for this ______ quality, though they note that al-Biruni's patience with his sources did not extend to flattering them.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: The quality historians value is the one just described: al-Biruni reported Indian views "in their own terms," left readers "to judge," and kept his own disagreements separate. The text contrasts this with "the far more partisan chronicles of the conquerors." A method that keeps feeling and bias out of the account is "dispassionate."
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Credulous" means too ready to believe. Al-Biruni recorded disagreements and did not flatter his sources, so he was not believing uncritically.
explanation.B: Correct. "Dispassionate" means free from bias or strong feeling, which fits reporting others' beliefs in their own terms and keeping one's own judgments separate.
explanation.C: Incorrect. "Cursory" means hasty and superficial, but al-Biruni "spent years" learning Sanskrit and questioning experts.
explanation.D: Incorrect. "Disparaging" means belittling. Although he did not flatter his sources, his stated aim was to report their views fairly and let readers judge, not to run them down.
